analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a date bump and new documentation for the `darkbloom sandbox setup` flow). The new documentation covers a disk-shortfall line (`SandboxSizingPlan.freeSpaceNote`, head lines 1092-1106) and a slot-change comparison on rerun (lines 1139-1156). Line 1217 documents installer exit status 4. No code, config, or control changes are present in the supplied evidence.

I checked the text against TB-013 and T-061, covering the installer download and add-on command. Lines 1051-1058 state that the CLI verifies the downloaded install.sh only via TLS, requiring HTTPS, a 1 MiB cap, a shell shebang, a 0600 file in a 0700 directory, and installer-side release verification. They say this openly. The newly documented behavior is a rerun on a set-up Mac that downloads the installer and runs `--plan` (lines 1141-1144). This reuses the same download and run path, and the documentation says the plan 'changes nothing'. It adds no new trust boundary, but it does increase how often the unverified installer script executes as the owner. That falls within the existing T-061 exposure, so I do not treat it as a regression.

Lines 1150-1151 document that the CLI applies slot changes automatically with `--yes`/no terminal only when slots are added and none removed. Line 1217 says the CLI never passes `--force`. Both are conservative.

The T-041/prefix-cache material in the status section is unchanged. No findings.

The next pass should confirm that the implementation in SandboxInstaller.swift and SandboxSetupCommand.swift matches the documented guards. Those files were not supplied here: the plan-before-install flow, the --force exclusion, and the apply-only-additions rule.
